svg.title: What QR codes, ArUco markers and fiducial objects present to an off-axis camera
svg.desc: Three panels along the top, each showing one marker type viewed from the same direction, 62 degrees away from square-on. The QR code fills its area with a dense grid of data modules and three corner finder patterns, because it is a storage format; at this angle the modules compress into each other. The ArUco marker carries only a short binary ID inside a thick black border, because its four outer corners are what a pose solver needs; the corners are still findable but the square is heavily foreshortened. Both flat markers present 47 percent of themselves at this angle. The fiducial object wraps a marker around every face of a dodecahedron, and one of its twelve faces is always turned towards the camera, presenting 96 percent here. The chart below plots this for every viewing angle: a flat marker follows a cosine and falls to nothing edge-on, while the dodecahedron never drops below 0.80, because some face is always within 37.3 degrees of square-on.
